Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFruitVege: Soured in a kraut barrel. Keeps two weeks out of the brine.
Tooltip_craft_DryingPoleDesc: A T-pole to hang garlic and onions in bunches or braids: in the air they cure half again as fast and keep a third longer. The place still decides.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFruitVege: Bulbs plaited by their own dry stalks: lighter to carry. Unbraid to use them; they keep and cure inside as loose ones do.
Tooltip_craft_HayCrateDesc: An open crate lined with hay: potatoes, sweet potatoes and pumpkins cure half again as fast in it, and potatoes, turnips, cabbages, sweet potatoes and pumpkins keep a third longer, on top of where it stands.
Tooltip_craft_SandCrateDesc: A crate of damp sand, the roots packed in layers with their tops showing: carrots, sugar beets, leeks and turnips keep a third longer, on top of where it stands.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFruitVege: Tomato paste under a salt crust. Spoon out a portion for a soup, stew or sauce.
Tomato paste under a salt crust and a cap of oil or fat: it keeps twice as long. Spoon out a portion for a soup, stew or sauce.
A spoonful of tomato paste, five tomatoes cooked down: a soup, stew, pasta or sauce tastes better for it. Keeps a week out of the crock.
Tomato paste scorched onto the pan. Scrape it out to get the pan back.
